standard_prerequisites.name: Morphisms of fibred categories preserve strongly cartesian morphisms
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Same chapter, the standing situation of a morphism of fibred categories over the base, whose defining property is the preservation of strongly cartesian morphisms
standard_prerequisites.use: Supplies that u o v' is the functor attached to p and U.

core_obligations: Construct the section for the source category (proof lines 9817-9822): let v' : D/V -> C'/U' be the functor built in the proof of the single-category lemma from p' and the object U'; since u preserves strongly cartesian morphisms, the functor v = u o v' is the corresponding functor for p and U.

Transfer the identities (proof lines 9823-9826): the single-category lemma applied to v' gives a morphism of topoi sigma' with pi'_{U'} o sigma' = id and (sigma')^{-1} = pi'_{U',*}; setting sigma = g' o sigma' and using the identification of v with u o v' gives pi_U o sigma = id and sigma^{-1} = pi_{U,*}, which is the assertion.
proof_roadmap: Build the section for the source fibration and identify its underlying functor with the composite through u.
Read off the four identities from the single-category lemma applied to both fibrations.
difficulty_reason: The lemma provides a section sigma' of the localised morphism pi'_{U'} and shows that the induced section of pi_U has the analogous properties (statement lines 9794-9814). The proof (proof lines 9816-9826) uses the functor constructed in the single-category case, notes that the composite through u is the corresponding functor for the second fibration because u preserves strongly cartesian morphisms, and transfers the four identities. H2: one construction plus one transfer, written out.
